transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. To get us started, could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

They... they sent me here. My lieutenant did. At the station, I was... I was just organizing the airway bags. I had to put them in a specific pattern. It was the right way. And I was... saying the dispatch numbers. Just out loud. He told me to stop and step away, but... I couldn't. If I broke the sequence, the whole bay would... it would go bad. I had to finish it.

When you feel the need to arrange the bags and say the numbers, do you feel like you are doing it because you want to, or does it feel like something you are forced to do against your will to prevent something terrible from happening?
I don't... I'm not really sure. I didn't think about it like that. I just... I just had to do it. That's all.
Have you ever been diagnosed with or told by a doctor that you have any repetitive, involuntary movements or sounds, like eye blinking, shrugging, or throat clearing?
No. Nobody's ever said anything like that to me. I don't... I don't do that.
Before you start arranging the bags and saying the numbers, do you have a recurring, unwanted thought or image in your mind that makes you feel like you need to do those things?
No... I don't think so. I just... I just know they need to be that way. There's no picture or anything. It's just... how it has to be.
When you are arranging the bags, is the primary reason you do it because they feel 'wrong' or 'imbalanced' until they are in that specific pattern?
Not really... I don't know about imbalanced. It's just... they go where they go. That's it.
What do you think would happen if you were interrupted and couldn't finish arranging the bags?

I don't know... I didn't want to find out. That's why I'm here, I guess. At the station, I was moving the airway bags. Putting them in the right pattern. I was saying the dispatch numbers out loud, just... repeating them. My lieutenant told me to stop, to step away, but... I wouldn't. I couldn't. If I broke the sequence, it just felt like... like the whole bay would go bad. So I didn't stop.
When you are repeating these dispatch numbers, do you feel a sense of internal pressure or a mental urge that you must repeat them a specific number of times until it feels 'just right'?
I don't think so. I don't count how many times I say them. I just... I just say them. There's no feeling of it being just right or anything... I just do it.
Are you currently taking any medications, or have you recently had any significant changes in your physical health, such as a head injury or a new medical diagnosis?
No. No medications. I'm fine... physically, I mean. No head injuries or anything like that. Just... no.
Does this need to arrange items and repeat these numbers happen in other places, like at your home or in other settings, or does it only happen when you are at the station working?
I don't really know... I guess mostly just at the station. I haven't really noticed doing it at home. Just... at work.

Have you noticed any other unusual changes, such as sudden shifts in your personality, problems with your memory, or unexplained physical sensations, that have started occurring around the same time as these behaviors at work?
No... I don't think so. My memory is fine. I haven't felt anything... physical. Just... no, nothing like that.
When you are performing these tasks at work, do you feel a sense of distress or anxiety if you are unable to complete them the way you believe they must be done?
I don't... no. I just do it. It's not... I don't get anxious about it or anything. I just do what I'm supposed to do.
When you are at the station and feel the need to arrange the bags or say the numbers, do you ever hear voices or sounds that no one else can hear telling you to do those things?
No... I don't hear anyone. It's just... I just know how it needs to be done. Nobody is telling me to.

When you say the bay would 'go bad' if you didn't finish the sequence, do you believe that something specific and harmful will actually happen to the building or the people there, or is it more of a vague, uncomfortable feeling that you can't quite explain?
I don't... I don't really know. It just goes bad. I can't really explain it. It's just... bad if I don't.
Do you feel that you have a special responsibility or a unique understanding about how the station must be maintained that your colleagues simply don't see or understand?

I don't... I don't know about special. I just know what's happening. The other guys, they don't see it, but... I know the injury review people and some of the supervisors are watching me. Through the cameras at the station. They say it's just routine paperwork, but... they're changing my triage notes. They're trying to make me look like I'm unsafe. I just... I know they are.
You mentioned that the supervisors are watching you and changing your notes; do you believe that they are doing this as part of a larger plan or conspiracy to discredit you or cause you harm?

I don't know about a... conspiracy. I just know what I told you. They tell me it's just routine paperwork when they pull my files, but... it isn't. They watch the station cameras and they change my notes to make me look unsafe. I don't... I don't know why. That's just what they're doing.

Aside from your concerns about the supervisors, have you noticed any other changes in how you think, such as feeling like your thoughts are being broadcasted to others, or feeling like your emotions have become significantly blunted or empty?

I don't... I don't know about thoughts being broadcasted. That doesn't happen. But... I don't know, I guess I don't really do much anymore. Most days I just sit in my apartment. There's trash in the corner... food just sitting in the fridge. I used to call the guys to play basketball, or... I used to cook. But I just... I can't get myself to care. Or start doing any of it. I just sit there.

When you think about the supervisors watching you and changing your notes, do you feel that there is a specific, organized reason or a hidden message they are trying to send you through these actions?

I don't know about a hidden message. I already said... they're just watching me. The injury review people, the supervisors... they use the cameras at the station. They say it's just routine paperwork, but they're changing my triage notes. They want to make me look unsafe. That's all I know.
